content.value:
Aṣṭāvakragītā, transcribed by Suryansu Ray from the Lucknow 1971 edition, with
                    corrections.

The printed edition from which this e-text was transcribed was written in the
                Devanāgarī script. The electronic text below is in a lossless transliteration using
                the Latin alphabet. The transliteration scheme used is the IAST (
The International Alphabet of Sanskrit Transliteration

). IAST differs in
                small ways from ISO 15919, but is preferred by most working Sanskrit scholars.
                Conversion of this file to ISO 15919 can be achieved by performing the following
                replacements throughout the file:
Text division is as Devanāgarī ("ityevam" not "ity evam".)

Initial vowel elision for avagraha is reversed and marked with a + sign: e.g.,
                "prathamo+adhyāyaḥ"

The e-text was typed by Suryamsu Ray personally from a reprint of the Lucknow
                    1971 edition. He notes:

Only one edition I could buy myself from
                        Munshiram Manoharlal Publisher Private Ltd., which is in Hindi with Hindi
                        commentary as follows: "

Ashtavakragita", with Hindi commentary by
                            Raibahadur Babu Zalim Singh, edited by Dr. Brijesh Kumar Shukla,
                            published by Tejkumar Bookdepot P. Ltd., Lucknow, UP, India.

I
                        wanted to have at least one more version of the text for comparison wherever
                        doubts arose. Many Ashrams publish ancient texts for their own need. From a
                        religious mela I procured one, whose printing and exposition is less that
                        desirable. However, it served me the purpose of pinpointing the errors, for
                        which I apply mainly chhandas and usual philosophical word combinations and
                        phrases.

children.translated_text: Chapter 1
|| Now begins the blessed <s>Aṣṭāvakra Gītā</s> ||
<s>Janaka</s> said ||1||
How is <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) attained? How will <s>mukti</s> (liberation) come about?

children.text: vairāgyaṃ ca kathaṃ prāptametadbrūhi mama prabho||1|1||
children.translated_text: And how is <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion) obtained? Tell me this, O Lord. ||1|1||
<s>Aṣṭāvakra</s> said ||
If you desire <s>mukti</s> (liberation), my child, shun sense-objects as poison,
and cultivate forgiveness, sincerity, compassion, contentment, and truth as nectar. ||1|2||

children.text: na pṛthvī na jalaṃ nāgnirna vāyurdyaurna vā bhavān|
children.translated_text: You are neither earth, nor water, nor fire, nor air, nor space,
know the <s>Ātman</s> (Self) as the witness of all these, of the nature of <s>Cit</s> (consciousness), for the sake of liberation. ||1|3||

children.text: yadi dehaṃ pṛthakkṛtya citi viśrāmya tiṣṭhasi|
children.translated_text: If you detach yourself from the body and rest in <s>Citi</s> (consciousness),
you will at once become happy, peaceful, and free from bondage. ||1|4||

children.text: na tvaṃ viprādiko varṇo nāśramī nākṣagocaraḥ|
children.translated_text: You are not a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> or any other <s>varṇa</s> (caste), you do not belong to any <s>āśrama</s> (stage of life), nor are you perceived by the senses.
You are unattached and formless, the witness of the universe — be happy. ||1|5||

children.text: dharmādharmau sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ mānasāni na te bibho|
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> (virtue) and <s>adharma</s> (vice), pleasure and pain are of the mind, not yours, O all-pervading one.

children.text: na kartā+asi na bhoktā+asi mukta evā+asi sarvadā||1|6||
children.translated_text: You are neither the doer nor the enjoyer — you are ever free indeed. ||1|6||
You are the one seer of all, and you are indeed always nearly free.

children.text: ayameva hi te bandho draṣṭāraṃ paśyasītaram||1|7||
children.translated_text: Your only bondage is this: that you see the seer as other than yourself. ||1|7||
Bitten by the great black serpent of ego-sense, thinking 'I am the doer,'

children.text: nāhaṃ karteti viśvāsāmṛtaṃ pītvā sukhī bhava||1|8||
children.translated_text: drink the nectar of the conviction 'I am not the doer,' and be happy. ||1|8||
With the fire of the conviction 'I am the one pure consciousness,'
burn down the forest of ignorance, and being free from sorrow, be happy. ||1|9||
That in which this universe appears, superimposed like a snake on a rope —
that is bliss, supreme bliss, that consciousness you are — live happily. ||1|10||
One who considers oneself free is indeed free; one who considers oneself bound is indeed bound.

children.text: kiṃvadantīha satyeyaṃ yā matiḥ sā gatirbhavet||1|11||
children.translated_text: The popular saying is true here: 'As one thinks, so one becomes.' ||1|11||

children.text: ātmā sākṣī vibhuḥ pūrṇa eko muktaścidakriyaḥ|
children.translated_text: The <s>Ātman</s> (Self) is the witness, all-pervading, complete, one, free, consciousness, actionless,
unattached, desireless, peaceful — it only appears as if in <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) through delusion. ||1|12||
Meditate on the <s>Ātman</s> (Self) as immutable, consciousness, non-dual,
having abandoned the illusion of being a mere reflection, and all notions external and internal. ||1|13||
For long have you been bound by the noose of identification with the body, O child.
Sever that with the sword of the knowledge 'I am consciousness,' and be happy. ||1|14||
You are unattached, actionless, self-luminous, and untainted.
This indeed is your bondage: that you practice <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption). ||1|15||

children.text: tvayā vyāptamidaṃ viśvaṃ tvayi protaṃ yathārthataḥ|
children.translated_text: By you is this universe pervaded; in you it is truly strung.
You are of the nature of pure consciousness — do not be small-minded. ||1|16||
Be free from expectation, free from modification, self-sufficient, of cool disposition,
of unfathomable intelligence, unperturbed — abide with <s>Cit</s> (consciousness) as your only inclination. ||1|17||
Know that which has form to be unreal, and the formless to be immutable.
Through this teaching of truth, there is no possibility of rebirth. ||1|18||
Just as a reflection exists within a mirror, yet the mirror pervades both inside and out,
so too the Supreme Lord exists within and all around this body. ||1|19||
Just as the one all-pervading space is both inside and outside a pot,
so the eternal, unbroken <s>Brahman</s> exists in all beings likewise. ||1|20||
Chapter 2
<s>Janaka</s> said ||2||

children.text: aho nirañjanaḥ śānto bodho+ahaṃ prakṛteḥ paraḥ|
children.translated_text: Ah! I am untainted, peaceful, consciousness, beyond <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature).
For all this time, I have been deceived by delusion alone. ||2|1||
Just as I alone illuminate this body, so too the world.

children.text: ato mama jagatsarvamathavā na ca kiñcana||2|2||
children.translated_text: Therefore either the whole universe is mine, or nothing at all is. ||2|2||
Ah! Having now abandoned the universe along with the body,
by some skill, the <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self) is perceived. ||2|3||
Just as waves, foam, and bubbles are not different from water,
so too the universe, which has emerged from the <s>Ātman</s> (Self), is not different from the <s>Ātman</s>. ||2|4||
Upon inquiry, a cloth is indeed nothing but thread,
so too, upon inquiry, this universe is nothing but the <s>Ātman</s> (Self). ||2|5||
Just as sugar produced from sugarcane juice is wholly pervaded by it,

children.text: tathā viśvaṃ mayi kḷptaṃ mayā vyāptaṃ nirantaram||2|6||
children.translated_text: so too the universe, produced in me, is pervaded by me without interruption. ||2|6||
From ignorance of the <s>Ātman</s> (Self) the world appears; from knowledge of the <s>Ātman</s> it does not appear,
from ignorance of the rope, a snake appears; from knowledge of it, it does not appear indeed. ||2|7||

children.text: prakāśo me nijaṃ rūpaṃ nātirikto+asmyahaṃ tataḥ|
children.translated_text: Light is my own nature — I am not other than that.

children.text: yadā prakāśate viśvaṃ tadā+ahambhāsa eva hi||2|8||
children.translated_text: When the universe shines forth, it is indeed I alone who shine. ||2|8||
Ah! The universe appears in me through ignorance, superimposed,

children.text: rūpyaṃ śuktau phaṇī rajjau vāri sūryakare yathā||2|9||
children.translated_text: like silver in a shell, like a snake in a rope, like water in a sunbeam. ||2|9||
The universe has arisen from me and will dissolve back into me alone,

children.text: mṛdi kumbho jale vīciḥ kanake kaṭakaṃ yathā||2|10||
children.translated_text: as a pot into clay, a wave into water, a bracelet into gold. ||2|10||

children.text: aho ahaṃ namo mahyaṃ vināśo yasya nāsti me|
children.translated_text: Ah! I bow to myself! For whom there is no destruction,
who persists even when the world from <s>Brahmā</s> down to a blade of grass is destroyed. ||2|11||
Ah! I bow to myself! I am one, though embodied,
neither going anywhere nor coming, yet pervading the universe I abide. ||2|12||

children.text: aho ahaṃ namo mahyaṃ dakṣo nāstīha matsamaḥ|
children.translated_text: Ah! I bow to myself! There is none as skilled as I,

children.text: asaṃspṛśya śarīreṇa yena viśvaṃ ciraṃ dhṛtam||2|13||
children.translated_text: who has sustained the universe for all time without even touching it with the body. ||2|13||

children.text: aho ahaṃ namo mahyaṃ yasya me nāsti kiñcana|
children.translated_text: Ah! I bow to myself, to whom nothing belongs,
or to whom everything belongs that is within the reach of speech and mind. ||2|14||

children.text: jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ tathā jñātā tritayaṃ nāsti vāstavam|
children.translated_text: Knowledge, the knowable, and the knower — this triad does not truly exist.
I am that stainless one in whom this triad appears through ignorance. ||2|15||
Ah! Duality is the root of suffering — there is no other remedy for it.
All this that is seen is unreal — I am one, of the essence of consciousness, and pure. ||2|16||
I am pure awareness alone — through ignorance, limiting adjuncts have been imagined by me.
Thus reflecting constantly, my abidance is in the unconditioned state. ||2|17||

children.text: aho mayi sthitaṃ viśvaṃ vastuto na mayi sthitam|
children.translated_text: Ah! The universe exists in me, yet in truth it does not exist in me.

children.text: na me bandho+asti mokṣo vā bhrāntiḥ śāntā nirāśrayā||2|18||
children.translated_text: I have neither bondage nor liberation — the illusion has come to rest, without any support. ||2|18||
This universe along with the body has been ascertained to be nothing.
The <s>Ātman</s> (Self) is pure consciousness alone — upon what then is there any imagining now? ||2|19||
The body, heaven and hell, bondage and liberation, as well as fear —
all this is mere imagination. What concern is any of it to me, whose nature is consciousness? ||2|20||

children.text: aho janasamūhe+api na dvaitaṃ paśyato mama|
children.translated_text: Ah! Even in the midst of a multitude of people, I see no duality.
It has become like a forest — in what shall I take delight? ||2|21||

children.text: nāhaṃ deho na me deho jīvo nāhamahaṃ hi cit|
children.translated_text: I am not the body, nor is the body mine; I am not the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) — I am <s>Cit</s> (consciousness).

children.text: ayameva hi me bandha āsīdyā jīvite spṛhā||2|22||
children.translated_text: This indeed was my bondage: the desire for life. ||2|22||
Ah! In me, the infinite ocean, the manifold waves of the universe arise suddenly,
as the wind of the mind stirs up. ||2|23||
In me, the infinite ocean, when the wind of the mind subsides,
the merchant-vessel of the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul), bearing the world, is wrecked by misfortune. ||2|24||
In me, the infinite ocean, how wonderful — the waves of <s>jīvas</s> (individual souls)
arise, clash, play, and merge back, according to their nature. ||2|25||
Chapter 3
<s>Aṣṭāvakra</s> said ||3||
Having truly known the <s>Ātman</s> (Self) to be indestructible and one,
how can you, steady in Self-knowledge, take delight in the acquisition of wealth? ||3|1||
Ah! From ignorance of the <s>Ātman</s> (Self) arises attachment to sense-objects, which are the domain of delusion,
just as from ignorance of the shell arises greed for the illusion of silver. ||3|2||

children.text: viśvaṃ sphurati yatredaṃ taraṅgā iva sāgare|
children.translated_text: This universe shines forth in which, like waves in the ocean —

children.text: so+ahamasmīti vijñāya kiṃ dīna iva dhāvasi||3|3||
children.translated_text: knowing 'I am That,' why do you run about like a wretched one? ||3|3||
Even after hearing that the <s>Ātman</s> (Self) is pure <s>Caitanya</s> (consciousness) and supremely beautiful,
one who remains excessively attached to sensual pleasures comes to defilement. ||3|4||
For the sage who knows the <s>Ātman</s> (Self) in all beings and all beings in the <s>Ātman</s>,
it is astonishing that the sense of 'mine' persists. ||3|5||
One who is established in supreme non-duality and is resolved upon <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) —
it is astonishing that such a one, subject to desire, is weakened by amorous play. ||3|6||
Having recognized that the enemy of <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) has arisen, and being exceedingly weak,
it is astonishing that one should desire pleasure even as the hour of death approaches. ||3|7||
For one who is dispassionate toward both this world and the next, who discriminates between the eternal and the transient —
it is astonishing that one desirous of <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) should be frightened of liberation itself. ||3|8||
But the wise one, whether feted or afflicted, at all times

children.text: ātmānaṃ kevalaṃ paśyanna tuṣyati na kupyati||3|9||
children.translated_text: sees only the <s>Ātman</s> (Self) alone — neither rejoices nor becomes angry. ||3|9||
The great-souled one sees one's own body acting as if it were another's body.
How would such a noble one be disturbed by praise or blame? ||3|10||
Seeing this universe as nothing but <s>Māyā</s> (illusion), having lost all curiosity,

children.text: api sannihite mṛtyau kathaṃ trasyati dhīradhīḥ||3|11||
children.translated_text: how would the steady-minded one tremble even when death is near? ||3|11||
The great soul whose mind is free from desire, even in utter hopelessness —
who can compare with one who is content in Self-knowledge? ||3|12||
One who knows by one's very nature that all this that is seen is nothing —

children.text: idaṃ grāhyamidaṃ tyājyaṃ sa kiṃ paśyati dhīradhīḥ||3|13||
children.translated_text: for such a steady-minded one, what is there to accept and what to reject? What does such a one see? ||3|13||
For one who has inwardly renounced all passions, who is free from the pairs of opposites and free from desires,

children.text: yadṛcchayā+a+agato bhogo na duḥkhāya na tuṣṭaye||3|14||
children.translated_text: enjoyment that comes of its own accord causes neither suffering nor satisfaction. ||3|14||
Chapter 4
<s>Janaka</s> said ||4||
Indeed, for the knower of the <s>Ātman</s> (Self), the courageous one who plays in the sport of enjoyment,
there is no similarity whatsoever with the deluded worldlings who carry the burden of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence). ||4|1||
That state which all the gods, beginning with <s>Indra</s>, longingly seek —

children.text: aho tatra sthito yogī na harṣamupagacchati||4|2||
children.translated_text: Ah, the <s>yogin</s> established there does not experience joy. ||4|2||
For one who knows That, no inner contact with merit or sin arises;
just as the sky has no connection with smoke, even though it appears [to be there]. ||4|3||
That great soul who has known this entire universe to be the <s>Ātman</s> (Self) alone,

children.text: yadṛcchayā vartamānaṃ taṃ niṣeddhuṃ kṣameta kaḥ||4|4||
children.translated_text: acting spontaneously — who could restrain him? ||4|4||
Among the fourfold host of beings, from <s>Brahmā</s> down to a blade of grass,
only the wise one has the capacity to be free from desire and aversion. ||4|5||
Someone knows the <s>Ātman</s> (Self) to be non-dual, the lord of the universe;

children.text: yadvetti tatsa kurute na bhayaṃ tasya kutracit||4|6||
children.translated_text: whatever he knows, that he does — there is no fear for him anywhere. ||4|6||
Chapter 5
<s>Aṣṭāvakra</s> said: ||5||

children.text: na te saṅgo+asti kenāpi kiṃ śuddhastyaktumicchasi|
children.translated_text: You have no attachment to anything — what [is it that] you, being pure, wish to renounce?
Dissolving the aggregate [of body and mind], thus indeed go to dissolution. ||5|1||
The universe arises from you as a bubble from the ocean;
knowing thus the <s>Ātman</s> (Self) to be one, thus indeed go to dissolution. ||5|2||
Though perceived, the universe does not exist in you who are pure, for it has no real substance,
like a snake in a rope — clearly [so]; thus indeed go to dissolution. ||5|3||
Equal in sorrow and happiness, complete, equal in hope and despair,
equal in life and death — thus indeed go to dissolution. ||5|4||
Chapter 6
<s>Janaka</s> said: ||6||
I am infinite like space; the world of nature is like a pot.

children.text: iti jñānaṃ tathaitasya na tyāgo na graho layaḥ||6|1||
children.translated_text: Such is this knowledge — there is neither renunciation, nor grasping, nor dissolution for it. ||6|1||
I am like the great ocean; the phenomenal world is like waves.

children.text: iti jñānaṃ tathaitasya na tyāgo na graho layaḥ||6|2||
children.translated_text: Such is this knowledge — there is neither renunciation, nor grasping, nor dissolution for it. ||6|2||
I am like mother-of-pearl; the creation of the universe is like [the appearance of] silver.

children.text: iti jñānaṃ tathaitasya na tyāgo na graho layaḥ||6|3||
children.translated_text: Such is this knowledge — there is neither renunciation, nor grasping, nor dissolution for it. ||6|3||
I am in all beings, and all beings are in me;

children.text: iti jñānaṃ tathaitasya na tyāgo na graho layaḥ||6|4||
children.translated_text: such is this knowledge — there is neither renunciation, nor grasping, nor dissolution for it. ||6|4||
Chapter 7
<s>Janaka</s> said: ||7||
In me, the infinite great ocean, the vessel of the universe drifts here and there,
driven by the wind of its own nature — I have no intolerance. ||7|1||
In me, the infinite great ocean, the wave of the universe naturally

children.text: udetu vāstamāyātu na me vṛddhirna ca kṣatiḥ||7|2||
children.translated_text: may rise or set — there is neither increase nor diminution for me. ||7|2||
In me, the infinite great ocean, 'the universe' is merely conceptual imagination;
supremely tranquil, formless — this alone is what I am established in. ||7|3||
The <s>Ātman</s> (Self) is not in objects, nor are objects in that infinite, spotless [Self];
thus unattached, desireless, peaceful — this alone is what I am established in. ||7|4||
Ah! I am pure consciousness alone; the universe is like a magic show.
How then, and where, could there be for me the imagination of what is to be rejected or accepted? ||7|5||
Chapter 8
<s>Aṣṭāvakra</s> said: ||8||

children.text: tadā bandho yadā cittaṃ kiñcidvāñchati śocati|
children.translated_text: Then there is bondage when the mind desires something, grieves over something,
releases something, grasps something, is pleased by something, or is angered. ||8|1||

children.text: tadā muktiryadā cittaṃ na vāñchati na śocati|
children.translated_text: Then there is liberation when the mind does not desire, does not grieve,

children.text: na muñcati na gṛhṇāti na hṛṣyati na kupyati||8|2||
children.translated_text: does not release, does not grasp, is not pleased, and is not angered. ||8|2||

children.text: tadā bandho yadā cittaṃ saktaṃ kāsvapi dṛṣṭiṣu|
children.translated_text: Then there is bondage when the mind is attached to any particular viewpoint;
then there is liberation when the mind is unattached to all viewpoints. ||8|3||

children.text: yadā nāhaṃ tadā mokṣo yadāhaṃ bandhanaṃ tadā|
children.translated_text: When there is no 'I,' there is liberation; when there is 'I,' there is bondage;

children.text: matveti helayā kiñcinmā gṛhāṇa vimuñca mā||8|4||
children.translated_text: knowing this, easily — neither grasp nor release anything! ||8|4||
Chapter 9
<s>Aṣṭāvakra</s> said: ||9||

children.text: kṛtākṛte ca dvandvāni kadā śāntāni kasya vā|
children.translated_text: The dualities of the done and the undone — when are they at rest, and for whom?
Knowing this, becoming dispassionate here, be devoted to renunciation, free from vows. ||9|1||
For some blessed one, O dear one, through observing the activities of the world,
the desire to live, the desire to eat, and the desire to know have come to rest. ||9|2||
All this is impermanent, tainted by the three kinds of suffering,
without essence, contemptible, and to be abandoned — having ascertained this, one becomes peaceful. ||9|3||

children.text: ko+asau kālo vayaḥ kiṃ vā yatra dvandvāni no nṛṇām|
children.translated_text: What time is there, what age, in which there are no dualities for people?
Disregarding them, acting according to what comes, one attains perfection. ||9|4||

children.text: nānā mataṃ maharṣīṇāṃ sādhūnāṃ yogināṃ tathā|
children.translated_text: The opinions of the great sages, saints, and <s>yogins</s> are various;

children.text: dṛṣṭvā nirvedamāpannaḥ ko na śāmyati mānavaḥ||9|5||
children.translated_text: seeing this, who among men, having attained dispassion, does not become peaceful? ||9|5||

children.text: kṛtvā mūrtiparijñānaṃ caitanyasya na kiṃ guruḥ|
children.translated_text: Is he not a <s>guru</s> (teacher) who, having brought about the recognition of consciousness as embodied form,
by the means of dispassion, equanimity, and reasoning, rescues one from <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration)? ||9|6||
Behold the modifications of the elements as nothing but elements, in their true nature;
at that very moment, freed from bondage, you will abide in your own true nature. ||9|7||

children.text: vāsanā eva saṃsāra iti sarvā vimuñca tāḥ|
children.translated_text: <s>Vāsanā</s> (latent impression) alone is <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of existence) — therefore release them all;
their renunciation is the renunciation of <s>vāsanā</s>; abide now as you are. ||9|8||
Chapter 10
<s>Aṣṭāvakra</s> said: ||10||
Having abandoned <s>kāma</s> (desire), the enemy, and <s>artha</s> (wealth), beset with calamity,
and even <s>dharma</s> (duty), the cause of both — practice indifference toward everything. ||10|1||
View as a dream or a magic show the three or five days [of life],
along with friends, lands, wealth, houses, wives, and gifts of fortune. ||10|2||

children.text: yatra yatra bhavettṛṣṇā saṃsāraṃ viddhi tatra vai|
children.translated_text: Wherever there is craving, know that to be <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence);
taking refuge in firm <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion), be free from craving and happy. ||10|3||
Bondage is nothing but craving itself; its destruction is called liberation.
Through mere non-attachment to worldly existence, contentment is attained again and again. ||10|4||
You are the one, conscious, pure; the universe is inert and unreal;

children.text: avidyāpi na kiñcitsā kā bubhutsā tathāpi te||10|5||
children.translated_text: <s>Avidyā</s> (ignorance) too is nothing — so what then is your desire to know? ||10|5||

children.text: rājyaṃ sutāḥ kalatrāṇi śarīrāṇi sukhāni ca|
children.translated_text: Kingdoms, sons, wives, bodies, and pleasures —
though you were attached [to them], they have perished for you in birth after birth. ||10|6||
Enough of wealth, enough of desire, enough even of meritorious action!
In the wilderness of <s>saṃsāra</s>, the mind has never found rest from these. ||10|7||

children.text: kṛtaṃ na kati janmāni kāyena manasā girā|
children.translated_text: Through how many births has action not been performed — by body, mind, and speech —
action that is the cause of suffering and toil? Let it cease even now! ||10|8||
Chapter 11
<s>Aṣṭāvakra</s> said: ||11||
Existence, non-existence, and modification arise from one's own nature — having this firm conviction,
free from modification, free from affliction, one becomes peaceful with ease. ||11|1||
The Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>) is the creator of all, there is no other here — having this firm conviction,
one whose inner hopes have all dissolved is peaceful and attached nowhere. ||11|2||
Adversities and fortunes come in their own time, by fate alone — having this firm conviction,

children.text: tṛptaḥ svasthendriyo nityaṃ na vāñchati na śocati||11|3||
children.translated_text: contented, with senses ever composed, one neither desires nor grieves. ||11|3||
Happiness and sorrow, birth and death are by fate alone — having this firm conviction,
seeing nothing to be accomplished, free from effort, even while acting, one is not tainted. ||11|4||
Suffering arises from thinking alone, and from nothing else — having this firm conviction,

children.text: tayā hīnaḥ sukhī śāntaḥ sarvatra galitaspṛhaḥ||11|5||
children.translated_text: free from thinking, happy, peaceful, with desire everywhere dissolved. ||11|5||

children.text: nāhaṃ deho na me deho bodho+ahamiti niścayī|
children.translated_text: I am not the body, nor is the body mine; I am awareness — having this firm conviction,
having as if attained <s>kaivalya</s> (absolute aloneness), one does not remember what was done or not done. ||11|6||
From <s>Brahmā</s> down to a blade of grass, I alone am — having this firm conviction,
free from conceptual thought, pure, peaceful, one is content whether one has obtained or not. ||11|7||
This manifold, wondrous universe is nothing — having this firm conviction,
free from <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impressions), being mere spontaneity, one becomes peaceful as if nothing [exists]. ||11|8||
Chapter 12
<s>Janaka</s> said: ||12||
First, intolerant of bodily activity; then, intolerant of expansive speech;
then, intolerant of thought — thus indeed I am established. ||12|1||
Through the absence of delight in sound and other [sense-objects], and through the invisibility of the <s>Ātman</s> (Self),
with a heart free from distraction and one-pointed — thus indeed I am established. ||12|2||
The effort of <s>samādhi</s> and such [practices] is a distraction; worldly activity is for <s>samādhi</s> [itself].
Having perceived the rule to be thus — thus indeed I am established. ||12|3||
Through the absence of what is to be rejected and what is to be accepted, and thus of joy and sorrow,
through their absence today, O <s>Brahman</s> — thus indeed I am established. ||12|4||
The stages of life (<s>āśrama</s>), renunciation of stages, meditation, the acceptance and rejection by the mind —
observing these to be mere conceptual thought — thus indeed I am established. ||12|5||
The performance of action is due to ignorance, just as is its cessation;
having properly understood this truth — thus indeed I am established. ||12|6||
Thinking about the unthinkable, one merely assumes the form of thought;
therefore, having abandoned that contemplation — thus indeed I am established. ||12|7||

children.text: evameva kṛtaṃ yena sa kṛtārtho bhavedasau|
children.translated_text: Whoever has done thus — he becomes one who has accomplished the goal.

children.text: evameva svabhāvo yaḥ sa kṛtārtho bhavedasau||12|8||
children.translated_text: Whoever is thus by nature — he [too] has accomplished the goal. ||12|8||
Chapter 13
<s>Janaka</s> said: ||13||
The contentment of possessing nothing is difficult to attain, even in a loincloth;
having abandoned both renunciation and acceptance, I abide as I please. ||13|1||

children.text: kutrāpi khedaḥ kāyasya jihvā kutrāpi khidyate|
children.translated_text: Somewhere the body suffers, somewhere the tongue is troubled,

children.text: manaḥ kutrāpi tattyaktvā puruṣārthe sthitaḥ sukham||13|2||
children.translated_text: somewhere the mind [is troubled] — having abandoned all that, I abide happily in the supreme goal. ||13|2||

children.text: kṛtaṃ kimapi naiva syāditi saṃcintya tattvataḥ|
children.translated_text: Having reflected in truth that nothing whatsoever is really done,
whatever comes to be done, having done it, I abide as I please. ||13|3||
The <s>yogins</s> embodied in the body are bound by notions of action, inaction, and compulsion;
through the absence of union and separation, I abide as I please. ||13|4||

children.text: arthānarthau na me sthityā gatyā na śayanena vā|
children.translated_text: Neither benefit nor harm comes to me through standing, going, or lying down;
therefore, standing, going, or sleeping, I abide as I please. ||13|5||

children.text: svapato nāsti me hāniḥ siddhiryatnavato na vā|
children.translated_text: There is no loss for me in sleeping, and no attainment through effort;
having abandoned both destruction and elation, I abide as I please. ||13|6||
Having observed again and again in various states the inconstancy of pleasant and such [experiences],
having abandoned both the auspicious and the inauspicious, I abide as I please. ||13|7||
Chapter 14
<s>Janaka</s> said: (14)
One who is by nature empty-minded, yet through inadvertence entertains thoughts of existence,

children.text: nidrito bodhita iva kṣīṇasaṃsaraṇo hi saḥ||14|1||
children.translated_text: he is like a sleeping man who has been awakened — his cycle of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) is truly exhausted. (14.1)

children.text: kva dhanāni kva mitrāṇi kva me viṣayadasyavaḥ|
children.translated_text: Where are riches, where are friends, where are the thieves of sense-objects for me?

children.text: kva śāstraṃ kva ca vijñānaṃ yadā me galitā spṛhā||14|2||
children.translated_text: Where is scripture, where is knowledge, when all desire has fallen away from me? (14.2)
Having known the witness-<s>Puruṣa</s>, the supreme <s>Ātman</s> (Self), the Lord,

children.text: nairāśye bandhamokṣe ca na cintā muktaye mama||14|3||
children.translated_text: in the hopelessness regarding both bondage and liberation, there is no anxiety for my freedom. (14.3)
For one who is inwardly void of mental constructs and outwardly moves freely as he pleases,
only those who are likewise can recognize his various states, as if he were a madman. (14.4)
Chapter 15
<s>Aṣṭāvakra</s> said: (15)
Through straightforward instruction, one of pure <s>sattva</s> (goodness) and intelligence attains fulfillment,
but another, though seeking knowledge for a lifetime, remains bewildered. (15.1)
<s>Mokṣa</s> (liberation) is dispassion toward sense-objects; bondage is relish for sensory pleasures.
This alone is true knowledge — now do as you wish. (15.2)
This realization of truth renders the eloquent, learned, and industrious person silent, inert, and still,
and therefore it is shunned by those who crave enjoyment. (15.3)

children.text: na tvaṃ deho na te deho bhoktā kartā na vā bhavān|
children.translated_text: You are not the body, nor is the body yours; you are neither the enjoyer nor the doer.

children.text: cidrūpo+asi sadā sākṣī nirapekṣaḥ sukhaṃ cara||15|4||
children.translated_text: You are pure consciousness, the eternal witness, without dependence — move about happily. (15.4)
Attachment and aversion are properties of the mind, and the mind is never yours.
You are free of mental constructs, you are awareness itself, changeless — move about happily. (15.5)
Recognizing the Self in all beings and all beings in the Self,
free from ego-sense and the notion of 'mine,' be happy. (15.6)

children.text: viśvaṃ sphurati yatredaṃ taraṅgā iva sāgare|
children.translated_text: That in which this universe arises, like waves in the ocean,
you are That alone, without doubt — O embodiment of consciousness, be free of affliction. (15.7)

children.text: śraddhatsva tāta śraddhatsva nātra mohaṃ kuruṣva bhoḥ|
children.translated_text: Have faith, dear one, have faith! Do not fall into delusion here.
You are the Lord whose very nature is knowledge, you are the <s>Ātman</s> (Self), beyond <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature). (15.8)
The body, enveloped by the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities of nature), stands, comes, and goes.
The <s>Ātman</s> (Self) neither goes nor comes — why do you grieve for it? (15.9)
Let the body endure until the end of the cosmic cycle, or let it depart this very day.

children.text: kva vṛddhiḥ kva ca vā hānistava cinmātrarūpiṇaḥ||15|10||
children.translated_text: Where is gain and where is loss for you, whose nature is pure consciousness alone? (15.10)
In you, the infinite great ocean, the wave of the universe naturally

children.text: udetu vā+astamāyātu na te vṛddhirna vā kṣatiḥ||15|11||
children.translated_text: rises or sets — there is neither increase nor diminishment for you. (15.11)

children.text: tāta cinmātrarūpo+asi na te bhinnamidaṃ jagat|
children.translated_text: Dear one, you are of the nature of pure consciousness alone; this world is not separate from you.
Therefore, for whom, how, and where can there be any notion of what is to be rejected or accepted? (15.12)
In the one imperishable, peaceful, stainless expanse of consciousness-space that is you,

children.text: kuto janma kuto karma kuto+ahaṃkāra eva ca||15|13||
children.translated_text: whence is birth, whence is action, whence even the sense of 'I'? (15.13)
Whatever you perceive, in all of that you alone shine forth.
Do bracelets, armlets, and anklets shine as something different from gold? (15.14)
Abandon the distinction 'this is I' and 'this I am not.'
Having ascertained that all is the Self, be free of intentions and be happy. (15.15)
It is only through your ignorance that the universe exists; in truth, you alone are.

children.text: tvatto+anyo nāsti saṃsārī nāsaṃsārī ca kaścana||15|16||
children.translated_text: There is no one other than you who is bound in <s>saṃsāra</s>, nor anyone who is free from it. (15.16)
This universe is nothing but delusion — nothing whatsoever exists; one who is firm in this conviction,
free from <s>vāsanās</s> (latent impressions), a mere flash of awareness, becomes still as if nothing at all. (15.17)
One alone was, is, and shall be in the ocean of existence.

children.text: na te bandho+asti mokṣo vā kṛtakṛtyaḥ sukhaṃ cara||15|18||
children.translated_text: There is neither bondage nor liberation for you — live happily, having fulfilled your purpose. (15.18)
Do not agitate the mind with fancies and counter-fancies, O one made of consciousness.
Be at peace and dwell happily in your own Self, whose very form is bliss. (15.19)

children.text: tyajaiva dhyānaṃ sarvatra mā kiñciddhṛdi dhāraya|
children.translated_text: Abandon meditation entirely; hold nothing whatsoever in the heart.

children.text: ātmā tvaṃ mukta evāsi kiṃ vimṛśya kariṣyasi||15|20||
children.translated_text: You are the <s>Ātman</s> (Self), ever free — what will you accomplish by deliberation? (15.20)
Chapter 16
<s>Aṣṭāvakra</s> said: (16)
You may recite or listen to various scriptures again and again, dear one,
yet you will not attain inner repose without forgetting everything. (16.1)

children.text: bhogaṃ karma samādhiṃ vā kuru vijña tathāpi te|
children.translated_text: You may pursue enjoyment, action, or <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption), O wise one, yet
the mind, stripped of all expectations, will delight exceedingly in that alone. (16.2)
Everyone is miserable through effort — no one understands this.
Through this instruction alone, the blessed one attains tranquility. (16.3)
One who feels weary even at the blinking and opening of the eyes,
happiness belongs to that champion of indolence and to no one else. (16.4)

children.text: idaṃ kṛtamidaṃ neti dvandvairmuktaṃ yadā manaḥ|
children.translated_text: When the mind is freed from the dualities of 'this has been done' and 'this has not been done,'
it becomes indifferent to <s>dharma</s> (duty), <s>artha</s> (wealth), <s>kāma</s> (pleasure), and <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation). (16.5)
The dispassionate one is averse to sense-objects; the passionate one is greedy for them.
But one free from both grasping and releasing is neither dispassionate nor attached. (16.6)
The notion of what is to be rejected and what is to be accepted is the sprout of the tree of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence),
and craving lives on as long as it provides a ground for the state of non-discrimination. (16.7)

children.text: pravṛttau jāyate rāgo nivṛttau dveṣa eva hi|
children.translated_text: In activity, attachment is born; in withdrawal, aversion arises.
The wise one, free from dualities, remains established like a child. (16.8)
One who is attached wishes to renounce <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) out of a desire to escape suffering,
but one free from attachment is without suffering and does not feel distressed even in it. (16.9)
One who has pride even regarding <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), and possessiveness toward the body,

children.text: na ca jñānī na vā yogī kevalaṃ duḥkhabhāgasau||16|10||
children.translated_text: is neither a <s>jñānī</s> (knower) nor a <s>yogī</s> (practitioner) — he is merely a partaker of suffering. (16.10)

children.text: haro yadyupadeṣṭā te hariḥ kamalajo+api vā|
children.translated_text: Even if <s>Hara</s> (Śiva) were your teacher, or <s>Hari</s> (Viṣṇu), or <s>Brahmā</s> the lotus-born,
still you will not attain inner repose without forgetting everything. (16.11)
Chapter 17
<s>Aṣṭāvakra</s> said: (17)
He has attained the fruit of knowledge, and likewise the fruit of <s>yoga</s> practice,

children.text: tṛptaḥ svacchendriyo nityamekākī ramate tu yaḥ||17|1||
children.translated_text: who, content and with senses naturally pure, ever delights in solitude. (17.1)
Never in this world does the knower of truth — alas — feel distressed,
for by him alone is this entire sphere of the universe filled. (17.2)

children.text: na jātu viṣayāḥ ke+api svārāmaṃ harṣayantyamī|
children.translated_text: None of these sense-objects ever delight one who revels in the Self,
just as neem leaves do not please an elephant that delights in <s>sallakī</s> (Boswellia) shoots. (17.3)
One who, when pleasures have been enjoyed, does not become habituated to them,
and when they remain unexperienced, has no longing — such a one is rare in the world. (17.4)
In this <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence), those desiring enjoyment and those desiring liberation are both seen,
but one who desires neither enjoyment nor liberation — that great soul is rare indeed. (17.5)
With regard to <s>dharma</s> (duty), <s>artha</s> (wealth), <s>kāma</s> (pleasure), <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), life, and death alike,
for one of noble mind, there is truly no notion of what is to be rejected or accepted. (17.6)

children.text: vāñchā na viśvavilaye na dveṣastasya ca sthitau|
children.translated_text: He has no desire for the dissolution of the universe, nor aversion to its continuance.
Therefore that blessed one lives happily, content with whatever livelihood comes. (17.7)
Fulfilled through this knowledge, with intellect dissolved and purpose accomplished,
he lives at ease — seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, and eating. (17.8)
His gaze is vacant, his actions purposeless, his senses incapacitated,
he has neither craving nor dispassion — the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) is dried up. (17.9)

children.text: na jāgarti na nidrāti nonmīlati na mīlati|
children.translated_text: He neither wakes nor sleeps, neither opens nor closes the eyes.
Ah, what a wondrous state exists for one whose mind is liberated! (17.10)
Everywhere he appears at ease, everywhere his disposition is pure.
Free from all <s>vāsanās</s> (latent impressions), the liberated one shines everywhere. (17.11)
Seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, taking, speaking, walking,
free from both striving and non-striving, the great soul is verily free. (17.12)

children.text: na nindati na ca stauti na hṛṣyati na kupyati|
children.translated_text: He neither blames nor praises, neither rejoices nor becomes angry,

children.text: na dadāti na gṛhṇāti muktaḥ sarvatra nīrasaḥ||17|13||
children.translated_text: he neither gives nor takes — the liberated one is dispassionate everywhere. (17.13)

children.text: sānurāgāṃ striyaṃ dṛṣṭvā mṛtyuṃ vā samupasthitam|
children.translated_text: Seeing a woman full of affection, or seeing death approaching,
with mind undisturbed and self-possessed, the great soul is verily free. (17.14)

children.text: sukhe duḥkhe nare nāryāṃ saṃpatsu vipatsu ca|
children.translated_text: In happiness and sorrow, in man and woman, in prosperity and adversity,
there is no distinction whatsoever for the steadfast one who sees equally everywhere. (17.15)

children.text: na hiṃsā naiva kāruṇyaṃ nauddhatyaṃ na ca dīnatā|
children.translated_text: There is no violence, no compassion, no arrogance, no humility,

children.text: nāścaryaṃ naiva ca kṣobhaḥ kṣīṇasaṃsaraṇe nare||17|16||
children.translated_text: no wonder, no agitation in one whose cycle of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) has been exhausted. (17.16)

children.text: na mukto viṣayadveṣṭā na vā viṣayalolupaḥ|
children.translated_text: The liberated one neither hates sense-objects nor craves them.
With mind ever unattached, he enjoys whatever comes, whether obtained or unobtained. (17.17)
The distinctions of concentration and distraction, benefit and harm,
the one whose mind is empty does not know — established as if in <s>kaivalya</s> (absolute aloneness). (17.18)
Free from 'mine,' free from ego-sense, certain that nothing exists,

children.text: antargalitasarvāśaḥ kurvannapi na lipyate [ karoti na ]||17|19||
children.translated_text: with all expectations dissolved within, he is untainted even while acting. (17.19)
Free from the states of mental illumination, delusion, dream, and torpor,
one whose mind has dissolved attains a certain indescribable state. (17.20)
Chapter 18
<s>Aṣṭāvakra</s> said: (18)
He upon whose awakening of knowledge, delusion becomes like a dream,
salutations to that radiance, peaceful and of the nature of bliss alone! (18.1)
One may acquire all worldly ends and attain abundant enjoyments,
yet one cannot become happy without the complete renunciation of everything. (18.2)
For one whose inner self is scorched by the blazing flames of the sun of obligatory duties,
whence can there be happiness without the cooling shower of the nectar of tranquility? (18.3)
This existence is mere mental projection — in ultimate reality, nothing exists.
There is no non-existence for things that have their own nature, yet which appear as both existent and non-existent. (18.4)

children.text: na dūraṃ na ca saṃkocāllabdhamevātmanaḥ padam|
children.translated_text: The state of the Self is neither far away nor attained through contraction;
it is beyond mental constructs, effortless, changeless, and unstained. (18.5)
With the mere cessation of delusion, through the mere recognition of one's own nature,
They shine, free from grief, with unobstructed vision. (18.6)
All [this] is mere imagination; the Self is free and eternal.

children.text: iti vijñāya dhīro hi kimabhyasyati bālavat||18|7||
children.translated_text: Knowing this, what does the wise one practice, like a child? (18.7)

children.text: ātmā brahmeti niścitya bhāvābhāvau ca kalpitau|
children.translated_text: Having ascertained that the Self is <s>Brahman</s>, and that existence and non-existence are imagined,

children.text: niṣkāmaḥ kiṃ vijānāti kiṃ brūte ca karoti kim||18|8||
children.translated_text: the desireless one — what does he know, what does he say, what does he do? (18.8)
'This I am,' 'this I am not' — such conceptualization has ceased.
For the <s>yogin</s> who has become silent, having ascertained that all is the Self — (18.9)

children.text: na vikṣepo na caikāgryaṃ nātibodho na mūḍhatā|
children.translated_text: there is neither distraction nor one-pointedness, neither excessive awareness nor stupor,

children.text: na sukhaṃ na ca vā duḥkhamupaśāntasya yoginaḥ||18|10||
children.translated_text: neither happiness nor suffering — for the <s>yogin</s> who has become serene. (18.10)

children.text: svārājye bhaikṣyavṛttau ca lābhālābhe jane vane|
children.translated_text: In sovereignty or in the life of begging, in gain or loss, among people or in the forest —
for the <s>yogin</s> whose nature is free from conceptualization, there is no difference. (18.11)

children.text: kva dharmaḥ kva ca vā kāmaḥ kva cārthaḥ kva vivekatā|
children.translated_text: Where is <s>dharma</s>, where desire, where wealth, where discrimination?
'This was done, this was not' — for the <s>yogin</s> freed from all pairs of opposites. (18.12)

children.text: kṛtyaṃ kimapi naivāsti na kā+api hṛdi rañjanā|
children.translated_text: There is no duty whatsoever to be done, nor any delight in the heart;
life itself simply goes on — for the <s>yogin</s> who is liberated while living (<s>jīvanmukta</s>). (18.13)

children.text: kva mohaḥ kva ca vā viśvaṃ kva taddhyānaṃ kva muktatā|
children.translated_text: Where is delusion, where the world, where meditation upon it, where liberation?
For the great soul who has come to rest at the boundary of all mental projections (<s>saṃkalpa</s>). (18.14)

children.text: yena viśvamidaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ sa nāstīti karotu vai|
children.translated_text: He by whom this world was seen may declare 'it does not exist';

children.text: nirvāsanaḥ kiṃ kurute paśyannapi na paśyati||18|15||
children.translated_text: but one free from desires (<s>nirvāsana</s>) — what will he do? Even seeing, he does not see. (18.15)

children.text: yena dṛṣṭaṃ paraṃ brahma so+ahaṃ brahmeti cintayet|
children.translated_text: He by whom the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> was seen might think 'I am <s>Brahman</s>';

children.text: kiṃ cintayati niścinto dvitīyaṃ yo na paśyati||18|16||
children.translated_text: but what does the thought-free one think, who does not see a second? (18.16)
He who has seen the distraction of the self undertakes restraint;
but the noble one is not distracted — in the absence of anything to be accomplished, what does he do? (18.17)
The wise one, though contrary to the world, lives as if in accord with the world;

children.text: na samādhiṃ na vikṣepaṃ na lepaṃ svasya paśyati||18|18||
children.translated_text: he sees in himself neither <s>samādhi</s> nor distraction nor attachment. (18.18)
The sage who is devoid of [notions of] existence and non-existence, content, free from desires —
he has truly done nothing, though to the world's eye he may appear to act. (18.19)

children.text: pravṛttau vā nivṛttau vā naiva dhīrasya durgrahaḥ|
children.translated_text: Whether in activity or in withdrawal, the wise one has no obstinate attachment;
whatever comes to be done at any time — having done it, he abides in happiness. (18.20)
Free from desires, without support, self-willed, freed from bondage,
tossed by the wind of residual impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>), he moves like a dry leaf. (18.21)

children.text: asaṃsārasya tu kvāpi na harṣo na viṣādatā|
children.translated_text: For one who is beyond <s>saṃsāra</s>, there is nowhere either joy or despondency;

children.text: sa śītalamanā nityaṃ videha iva rājate||18|22||
children.translated_text: with a mind always cool, he shines as if bodiless (<s>videha</s>). (18.22)

children.text: kutrāpi na jihāsāsti hāśā vāpi na kutracit|
children.translated_text: Nowhere is there a desire to abandon, nor a wish for anything anywhere —
for the wise one who delights in the Self (<s>ātmārāma</s>), whose nature is cool, pure, and transparent. (18.23)
For the one whose mind is empty by nature, who acts spontaneously,
the wise one, natural [in conduct] — there is neither pride nor humiliation. (18.24)

children.text: kṛtaṃ dehena karmedaṃ na mayā śuddharūpiṇā|
children.translated_text: 'This action was done by the body, not by me, who am of pure nature' —

children.text: iti cintānurodhī yaḥ kurvannapi karoti na||18|25||
children.translated_text: whoever follows this conviction, even while acting, does not act. (18.25)
He acts as if speaking of what is not real, yet he is not foolish;
the <s>jīvanmukta</s> (one liberated while living) is happy, glorious, and shines even while wandering in <s>saṃsāra</s>. (18.26)
Wearied by the many inquiries, the wise one has come to rest;

children.text: na kalpate na jānāti na śṛṇoti na paśyati||18|27||
children.translated_text: he neither imagines, nor knows, nor hears, nor sees. (18.27)
Being neither in <s>samādhi</s> nor in distraction, he is neither a seeker of liberation nor otherwise;
having ascertained that the perceived is imagined, he abides as <s>Brahman</s> alone — the great-souled one. (18.28)

children.text: yasyāntaḥ syādahaṃkāro na karoti karoti saḥ|
children.translated_text: He who has ego (<s>ahaṃkāra</s>) within — even not acting, he acts;
but by the wise one free from ego, nothing remains undone even though [outwardly] done. (18.29)
Neither agitated nor content, not a doer, free from movement,
without expectation, free from doubt — the mind of the liberated one shines. (18.30)

children.text: nirdhyātuṃ ceṣṭituṃ vāpi yaccittaṃ na pravartate|
children.translated_text: The mind that does not engage in meditation or action —
yet without cause it meditates and acts. (18.31)
A dull person, hearing the truth as it is, attains bewilderment;
or else, one who is not dull attains a state of contraction, appearing like one who is dull. (18.32)
One-pointedness and restraint are practiced intensely by the deluded;

children.text: dhīrāḥ kṛtyaṃ na paśyanti suptavatsvapade sthitāḥ||18|33||
children.translated_text: the wise see no duty to be done, established in their own state like one asleep. (18.33)
Whether through effort or without effort, the dull one does not attain satisfaction;
by the mere ascertainment of truth, the wise one becomes satisfied. (18.34)

children.text: śuddhaṃ buddhaṃ priyaṃ pūrṇaṃ niṣprapañcaṃ nirāmayam|
children.translated_text: Pure, awakened, beloved, complete, beyond phenomenal proliferation, free from disease —

children.text: ātmānaṃ taṃ na jānanti tatrābhyāsaparā janāḥ||18|35||
children.translated_text: people devoted to practice do not know that Self; therein [lies their error]. (18.35)
The deluded one does not attain liberation through action in the form of practice;
the blessed one, by mere knowledge, remains liberated and without modification. (18.36)
The dull one does not attain <s>Brahman</s> because he desires to become [it];
but the wise one, even without desiring, partakes of the nature of Supreme <s>Brahman</s>. (18.37)
The deluded, without foundation, busy with grasping, nourish <s>saṃsāra</s>;
the wise have cut the very root of this root of calamity. (18.38)

children.text: na śāntiṃ labhate mūḍho yataḥ śamitumicchati|
children.translated_text: The dull one does not find peace because he desires to become peaceful;
the wise one, having ascertained the truth, is always peaceful in mind. (18.39)
Where is the vision of the Self for one who depends on what is seen?
The wise do not see that [external]; they see the imperishable Self. (18.40)

children.text: kva nirodho vimūḍhasya yo nirbandhaṃ karoti vai|
children.translated_text: Where is restraint for the dull one who indeed makes effort at suppression?
For the wise one who delights in the Self, it is always natural and effortless. (18.41)
Some are thinkers of existence, others think of nothing at all;
but one who is free from thinking of both — that one alone is undisturbed. (18.42)
Those of deficient understanding meditate upon the Self as pure and non-dual,
but they do not know [it] due to delusion; they remain unsatisfied for their entire lives. (18.43)
The intellect of the seeker of liberation does not exist without a support;
but the intellect of the liberated one is always without support and without desire. (18.44)
Seeing the tigers of sense-objects, the frightened ones seeking refuge
quickly enter the cave [of restraint] for the attainment of suppression and one-pointedness. (18.45)
Seeing the lion free from desires (<s>Hari</s>), the elephants of sense-objects
flee silently — unable [to approach], they serve him with flattery. (18.46)
The one who is free from doubt, with a composed mind, does not maintain the practice of liberation;
seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, and eating — he abides in comfort. (18.47)
By merely hearing the truth, [one of] pure intellect becomes undisturbed;
he sees neither right conduct, nor misconduct, nor indifference. (18.48)
Whatever comes to be done at any time, that he does straightforwardly —

children.text: śubhaṃ vāpyaśubhaṃ vāpi tasya ceṣṭā hi bālavat||18|49||
children.translated_text: whether auspicious or inauspicious — his behavior is like that of a child. (18.49)
Through freedom he attains happiness; through freedom he attains the Supreme;
through freedom he goes to bliss; through freedom [he attains] the highest state. (18.50)
When one considers the Self as neither doer nor enjoyer,
then indeed all the modifications of the mind (<s>cittavṛtti</s>) come to an end. (18.51)
The state of the wise one shines, even if unruly in outward form;
but the artificial peace of the dull-minded one with a craving mind does not [shine]. (18.52)
Enjoying great pleasures, or entering mountain caves —
the wise, free from conceptualization, unbound, with liberated minds. (18.53)
Seeing a learned <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, a deity, a sacred place, a woman, a king, or a beloved one —

children.text: dṛṣṭvā saṃpūjya dhīrasya na kāpi hṛdi vāsanā||18|54||
children.translated_text: in the heart of the wise one, there is no desire whatsoever. (18.54)
Though mocked by servants, sons, wives, grandchildren, and kinsmen —

children.text: vihasya dhikkṛto yogī na yāti vikṛtiṃ manāk||18|55||
children.translated_text: the <s>yogin</s>, laughing, is not disturbed in the slightest. (18.55)

children.text: santuṣṭo+api na santuṣṭaḥ khinno+api na ca khidyate|
children.translated_text: Though content, he is not [attached to being] content; though pained, he is not [truly] pained;

children.text: tasyāścaryadaśāṃ tāṃ tāṃ tādṛśā eva jānate||18|56||
children.translated_text: those wondrous states — only those of like nature can know them. (18.56)

children.text: kartavyataiva saṃsāro na tāṃ paśyanti sūrayaḥ|
children.translated_text: The sense of duty-to-be-done is <s>saṃsāra</s>; the seers do not see it;
they are void in form, formless, changeless, free from disease. (18.57)
The dull-witted one, even while doing nothing, is agitated everywhere due to mental turbulence;

children.text: kurvannapi tu kṛtyāni kuśalo hi nirākulaḥ||18|58||
children.translated_text: but the skilful one, even while performing duties, is truly undisturbed. (18.58)

children.text: sukhamāste sukhaṃ śete sukhamāyāti yāti ca|
children.translated_text: He sits happily, sleeps happily, comes and goes happily,

children.text: sukhaṃ vakti sukhaṃ bhuṅkte vyavahāre+api śāntadhīḥ||18|59||
children.translated_text: speaks happily, eats happily — the one whose mind is peaceful, even in worldly dealings. (18.59)
He who, by nature, has no pain, even while engaging with the world like [others] —
like a great lake, unshakable, free from afflictions — he shines. (18.60)
Even from withdrawal, activity arises for the deluded;
but even the activity of the wise one yields the fruit of withdrawal. (18.61)
Dispassion toward possessions is generally seen in the dull;

children.text: dehe vigalitāśasya kva rāgaḥ kva virāgatā||18|62||
children.translated_text: for one from whom hope regarding the body has fallen away — where is attachment, where dispassion? (18.62)
The vision of the deluded is always attached to meditation or non-meditation;
but for the one who is self-established, that [vision] is of the nature of non-seeing, through the very thing to be meditated upon. (18.63)
The sage who moves desirelessly in all undertakings, like a child —
no stain attaches to that pure one, even while <s>karma</s> is being performed. (18.64)

children.text: sa eva dhanya ātmajñaḥ sarvabhāveṣu yaḥ samaḥ|
children.translated_text: Blessed indeed is that knower of the Self who is equal in all states —
seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating — with a mind free from craving. (18.65)

children.text: kva saṃsāraḥ kva cābhāsaḥ kva sādhyaṃ kva ca sādhanam|
children.translated_text: Where is <s>saṃsāra</s>, where appearance, where the goal, where the means?
For the wise one, always free from conceptualization, like the sky itself. (18.66)
He triumphs — the renouncer of [the pursuit of] objects, whose embodiment is of full, natural resonance;
One whose <s>samādhi</s> (absorption) abides in the unconditioned and unlimited, effortlessly — (18.67)
What more need be said? The great-souled one who has known the truth,
desiring neither enjoyment nor liberation, is always and everywhere dispassionate. (18.68)
This world of duality, beginning with <s>mahat</s> (the great principle), is a mere display of names;
having abandoned [it], what remains to be done for one of pure awareness? (18.69)
One who is certain that all this is an illusion and that nothing exists,
pure, with imperceptible radiance, by his very nature becomes peaceful. (18.70)
For one whose nature is the shining forth of pure [consciousness], who sees no reality in what is perceived —

children.text: kva vidhiḥ kva ca vairāgyaṃ kva tyāgaḥ kva śamo+api vā||18|71||
children.translated_text: where is injunction, where is renunciation, where is abandonment, and where even is tranquility? (18.71)
For one who shines forth in infinite form and who does not see <s>Prakṛti</s> (material nature) —

children.text: kva bandhaḥ kva ca vā mokṣaḥ kva harṣaḥ kva viṣādatā||18|72||
children.translated_text: where is bondage, where is liberation, where is joy, and where is sorrow? (18.72)
In <s>saṃsāra</s>, which extends only as far as the intellect, only <s>māyā</s> (illusion) revolves;
without possessiveness, without ego, desireless — the wise one shines. (18.73)
For the sage who sees the Self as imperishable and free from affliction —

children.text: kva vidyā kva ca vā viśvaṃ kva deho+ahaṃ mameti vā||18|74||
children.translated_text: where is knowledge, where is the universe, where is the body, and where is 'I' or 'mine'? (18.74)
If the dull-minded one abandons activities such as restraint and the like,
he immediately takes up fantasies and idle prattle. (18.75)

children.text: mandaḥ śrutvāpi tadvastu na jahāti vimūḍhatām|
children.translated_text: The dull one, even having heard the truth, does not abandon delusion;
though [appearing] free from conceptual construction outwardly through effort, inwardly he craves sense-objects. (18.76)
One whose actions have fallen away through knowledge, though in the world's view he is an actor,
finds no occasion to do or even to say anything. (18.77)

children.text: kva tamaḥ kva prakāśo vā hānaṃ kva ca na kiñcana|
children.translated_text: Where is darkness, where is light, where is cessation? There is nothing whatsoever
for the steadfast one who is changeless and free from anxiety at all times. (18.78)

children.text: kva dhairyaṃ kva vivekitvaṃ kva nirātaṅkatā+api vā|
children.translated_text: Where is patience, where is discrimination, and where even is freedom from anxiety
for the <s>yogī</s> whose nature is inexpressible and who is without any [fixed] nature? (18.79)

children.text: na svargo naiva narako jīvanmuktirna caiva hi|
children.translated_text: There is no heaven, nor indeed hell, nor even <s>jīvanmukti</s> (liberation while living);
what more need be said? From the perspective of <s>yoga</s>, there is nothing at all. (18.80)
He does not wish for gain, nor does he grieve over loss;
the mind of the steadfast one is cool, as if filled with nectar. (18.81)

children.text: na śāntaṃ stauti niṣkāmo na duṣṭamapi nindati|
children.translated_text: The desireless one does not praise the peaceful, nor does he censure the wicked;
equal in suffering and happiness, content — he sees nothing that needs to be done. (18.82)

children.text: dhīro na dveṣṭi saṃsāramātmānaṃ na didṛkṣati|
children.translated_text: The steadfast one does not hate <s>saṃsāra</s>, nor does he wish to see the Self;

children.text: harṣāmarṣavinirmukto na mṛto na ca jīvati||18|83||
children.translated_text: free from joy and indignation, he is neither dead nor alive. (18.83)
Without attachment to children and wife, desireless regarding sense-objects,
unconcerned even about his own body, without expectation — the wise one shines. (18.84)
Contentment [is found] everywhere for the steadfast one who lives as things happen,
who wanders wherever he pleases and sleeps wherever the sun sets. (18.85)

children.text: patatūdetu vā deho nāsya cintā mahātmanaḥ|
children.translated_text: Let the body fall or rise — the great-souled one has no concern about it,
having forgotten all <s>saṃsāra</s> through resting in the ground of his own nature. (18.86)
Possessing nothing, moving freely, free from dualities, with doubts severed,
unattached to all states of being — the wise one delights in solitude. (18.87)
Without possessiveness, the steadfast one shines, to whom a clod, a stone, and gold are equal,
the knot of the heart well-severed, <s>rajas</s> (passion) and <s>tamas</s> (inertia) shaken off. (18.88)
For one who is heedless everywhere, no desire (<s>vāsanā</s>) [remains] in the heart;
the liberated, satisfied Self — with whom can [such a one] be compared? (18.89)

children.text: jānannapi na jānāti paśyannapi na paśyati|
children.translated_text: Knowing, yet he does not know; seeing, yet he does not see;

children.text: bruvannapi na ca brūte ko+anyo nirvāsanādṛte||18|90||
children.translated_text: speaking, yet he does not speak — who else [is like this] except one free from latent tendencies (<s>vāsanā</s>)? (18.90)

children.text: bhikṣurvā bhūpatirvāpi yo niṣkāmaḥ sa śobhate|
children.translated_text: Whether a mendicant (<s>bhikṣu</s>) or a king — whoever is desireless, he shines;
one in whom the notion of auspicious and inauspicious has dissolved regarding all states of being. (18.91)

children.text: kva svācchandyaṃ kva saṃkocaḥ kva vā tattvaviniścayaḥ|
children.translated_text: Where is freedom, where is restriction, and where is the ascertainment of truth
for the <s>yogī</s> who has accomplished his purpose, whose nature is guileless simplicity? (18.92)
By one who is satisfied in the repose of the Self, who is without expectation, whose pain is gone —
that which is experienced within — how and to whom can it be told? (18.93)

children.text: supto+api na suṣuptau ca svapne+api śayito na ca|
children.translated_text: Even in sleep, he is not in deep sleep; even in dream, he is not lying down;

children.text: jāgare+api na jāgarti dhīrastṛptaḥ pade pade||18|94||
children.translated_text: even in waking, the steadfast one does not wake — satisfied at every step. (18.94)
The knower, though with thought, is thoughtless; though with senses, is without senses;
though with intellect, is without intellect; though with ego, is without ego-sense. (18.95)

children.text: na sukhī na ca vā duḥkhī na virakto na saṅgavān|
children.translated_text: Neither happy nor unhappy, neither detached nor attached,

children.text: na mumukṣurna vā mukto na kiñcinna ca kiñcana||18|96||
children.translated_text: neither seeking liberation nor liberated — he is neither something nor nothing. (18.96)

children.text: vikṣepe+api na vikṣiptaḥ samādhau na samādhimān|
children.translated_text: Even in distraction, he is not distracted; in <s>samādhi</s>, he has no [state of] <s>samādhi</s>;

children.text: jāḍye+api na jaḍo dhanyaḥ pāṇḍitye+api na paṇḍitaḥ||18|97||
children.translated_text: even in stupor, the blessed one is not stupid; even in learning, he is not a scholar. (18.97)
Liberated, at ease in whatever state, content with duty accomplished,
equal everywhere through desirelessness — he does not remember what was done or left undone. (18.98)

children.text: na prīyate vandyamāno nindyamāno na kupyati|
children.translated_text: He is not pleased when praised, nor angered when blamed;
he neither dreads death nor rejoices in life. (18.99)
The tranquil-minded one does not rush to crowded places, nor to the forest;
in whatever way, wherever — he remains the same. (18.100)
Chapter 19
<s>Janaka</s> said: (19)
With the pincers of the knowledge of truth, from the cavity of the heart,
I have extracted the thorn of the manifold conceptual grasping. (19.1)

children.text: kva dharmaḥ kva ca vā kāmaḥ kva cārthaḥ kva vivekatā|
children.translated_text: Where is <s>dharma</s>, where is desire (<s>kāma</s>), where is wealth (<s>artha</s>), and where is discrimination

children.text: kva dvaitaṃ kva ca vā+advaitaṃ svamahimni sthitasya me||19|2||
children.translated_text: for me who abide in my own glory? Where is duality, and where is non-duality? (19.2)

children.text: kva bhūtaṃ kva bhaviṣyadvā vartamānamapi kva vā|
children.translated_text: Where is the past, where the future, or where even the present?

children.text: kva deśaḥ kva ca vā nityaṃ svamahimni sthitasya me||19|3||
children.translated_text: Where is space, and where is eternity — for me who abide in my own glory? (19.3)

children.text: kva cātmā kva ca vā+anātmā kva śubhaṃ kvāśubhaṃ tathā|
children.translated_text: Where is the Self, where the non-self, where the auspicious, and where the inauspicious?

children.text: kva cintā kva ca vā+acintā svamahimni sthitasya me||19|4||
children.translated_text: Where is anxiety, and where freedom from anxiety — for me who abide in my own glory? (19.4)

children.text: kva svapnaḥ kva suṣuptirvā kva ca jāgaraṇaṃ tathā|
children.translated_text: Where is dream, where is deep sleep, and where likewise is waking?

children.text: kva turīyaṃ bhayaṃ vā+api svamahimni sthitasya me||19|5||
children.translated_text: Where is the fourth state (<s>turīya</s>), and where even is fear — for me who abide in my own glory? (19.5)

children.text: kva dūraṃ kva samīpaṃ vā bāhyaṃ kvābhyantaraṃ kva vā|
children.translated_text: Where is the far, where is the near, where the outer, and where the inner?

children.text: kva sthūlaṃ kva ca vā sūkṣmaṃ svamahimni sthitasya me||19|6||
children.translated_text: Where is the gross, and where the subtle — for me who abide in my own glory? (19.6)

children.text: kva mṛtyurjīvitaṃ vā kva lokāḥ kvāsya kva laukikam|
children.translated_text: Where is death and where life, where are the worlds, and where worldly affairs?

children.text: kva layaḥ kva samādhirvā svamahimni sthitasya me||19|7||
children.translated_text: Where is dissolution, and where is <s>samādhi</s> — for me who abide in my own glory? (19.7)
Enough of talk about the three goals of life (<s>trivarga</s>)! Enough of talk about <s>yoga</s>!
Enough of talk about knowledge — for me who am at rest in the Self! (19.8)
Chapter 20
<s>Janaka</s> said: (20)

children.text: kva bhūtāni kva deho vā kvendriyāṇi kva vā manaḥ|
children.translated_text: Where are the elements, where the body, where the senses, and where the mind?

children.text: kva śūnyaṃ kva ca nairāśyaṃ matsvarūpe nirañjane||20|1||
children.translated_text: Where is the void, and where is despair — in my own nature, which is stainless? (20.1)

children.text: kva śāstraṃ kvātmavijñānaṃ kva vā nirviṣayaṃ manaḥ|
children.translated_text: Where is scripture, where is self-knowledge, and where is the mind free from objects?

children.text: kva tṛptiḥ kva vitṛṣṇatvaṃ gatadvandvasya me sadā||20|2||
children.translated_text: Where is contentment, and where is desirelessness — for me who have always gone beyond duality? (20.2)

children.text: kva vidyā kva ca vā+avidyā kvāhaṃ kvedaṃ mama kva vā|
children.translated_text: Where is knowledge, and where is ignorance? Where is 'I,' where is 'this,' and where is 'mine'?

children.text: kva bandhaḥ kva ca vā mokṣaḥ svarūpasya kva rūpatā||20|3||
children.translated_text: Where is bondage, and where is liberation? Where is the form of one's own nature? (20.3)

children.text: kva prārabdhāni karmāṇi jīvanmuktirapi kva vā|
children.translated_text: Where are the commenced <s>karmas</s> (<s>prārabdha</s>), and where even is <s>jīvanmukti</s> (liberation while living)?
Where is that bodiless aloneness (<s>videhakaivalya</s>) — for me who am always without distinctions? (20.4)

children.text: kva kartā kva ca vā bhoktā niṣkriyaṃ sphuraṇaṃ kva vā|
children.translated_text: Where is the doer, and where the enjoyer? Where is the actionless shining forth?

children.text: kvāparokṣaṃ phalaṃ vā kva niḥsvabhāvasya me sadā||20|5||
children.translated_text: Where is the immediate result — for me who am always without any inherent nature? (20.5)

children.text: kva lokaṃ kva mumukṣurvā kva yogī jñānavānkva vā|
children.translated_text: Where is the world, where the seeker of liberation, where the <s>yogī</s>, and where the knower?

children.text: kva baddhaḥ kva ca vā muktaḥ svasvarūpe+ahamadvaye||20|6||
children.translated_text: Where is the bound one, and where the liberated — in my own nature, which is non-dual? (20.6)

children.text: kva sṛṣṭiḥ kva ca saṃhāraḥ kva sādhyaṃ kva ca sādhanam|
children.translated_text: Where is creation, and where is dissolution? Where is the goal, and where the means?
Where is the seeker, and where is attainment — in my own nature, which is non-dual? (20.7)

children.text: kva pramātā pramāṇaṃ vā kva prameyaṃ kva ca pramā|
children.translated_text: Where is the knower, where the means of knowledge, where the object of knowledge, and where is knowledge itself?

children.text: kva kiñcitkva na kiñcidvā sarvadā vimalasya me||20|8||
children.translated_text: Where is anything, and where is nothing — for me who am always pure? (20.8)

children.text: kva vikṣepaḥ kva caikāgryaṃ kva nirbodhaḥ kva mūḍhatā|
children.translated_text: Where is distraction, where is one-pointedness? Where is dullness, and where delusion?

children.text: kva harṣaḥ kva viṣādo vā sarvadā niṣkriyasya me||20|9||
children.translated_text: Where is joy, and where is sorrow — for me who am always actionless? (20.9)

children.text: kva caiṣa vyavahāro vā kva ca sā paramārthatā|
children.translated_text: Where is this empirical transaction, and where that ultimate reality?

children.text: kva sukhaṃ kva ca vā duḥkhaṃ nirvimarśasya me sadā||20|10||
children.translated_text: Where is happiness, and where is suffering — for me who am always free from deliberation? (20.10)

children.text: kva māyā kva ca saṃsāraḥ kva prītirviratiḥ kva vā|
children.translated_text: Where is <s>māyā</s> (illusion), and where is <s>saṃsāra</s>? Where is love, and where dispassion?

children.text: kva jīvaḥ kva ca tadbrahma sarvadā vimalasya me||20|11||
children.translated_text: Where is the individual soul (<s>jīva</s>), and where is <s>Brahman</s> — for me who am always pure? (20.11)

children.text: kva pravṛttirnivṛttirvā kva muktiḥ kva ca bandhanam|
children.translated_text: Where is activity, and where cessation? Where is liberation, and where bondage?
For me who am always immutable, undivided, and at ease — (20.12)

children.text: kvopadeśaḥ kva vā śāstraṃ kva śiṣyaḥ kva ca vā guruḥ|
children.translated_text: Where is instruction, where scripture? Where is the disciple, and where the teacher?

children.text: kva cāsti puruṣārtho vā nirupādheḥ śivasya me||20|13||
children.translated_text: Where even is the goal of human life — for me who am auspicious (<s>Śiva</s>) and without limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>)? (20.13)

children.text: kva cāsti kva ca vā nāsti kvāsti caikaṃ kva ca dvayam|
children.translated_text: Where does [anything] exist, and where does it not? Where is the one, and where the two?
What more need be said? Nothing whatsoever arises for me. (20.14)
Thus [ends] the glorious <s>Aṣṭāvakragītā</s>.
